sources.news_title: JUST IN: Car Crash Leaves Alaska Democrat Senate Hopeful Mary Peltola Injured – 100PercentFedUp.com – by Jack
sources.text:
Former Alaska Rep. Mary Peltola and members of her family suffered minor injuries Saturday night after another driver struck the vehicle carrying them to a major gathering in Anchorage, her campaign announced Sunday.
The Democrat was on her way to the Alaska Federation of Natives Annual Banquet when the crash happened.
Peltola and her family needed medical attention, but the campaign said their injuries were minor and that everyone was in good spirits.
Medical providers advised Peltola to take time to recover, prompting her campaign to reschedule Sunday and Monday stops in Fairbanks and Bethel on the Alaska Always Tour.
“Mary looks forward to being back on the road soon and continuing to visit every corner of the state,” the campaign said in its public statement.
Peltola Campaign Statement on Upcoming Campaign Stops in Fairbanks and Bethel for the Alaska Always Tour: pic.twitter.com/ZhIzk3Oipk
— Mary Peltola (@MaryPeltola) October 25, 2026
The statement did not identify the other driver, give the precise location of the collision, or describe the vehicles involved.
It also did not say that Peltola had been hospitalized.
That distinction matters. The information released so far supports reporting that Peltola was injured and received medical attention, but it does not support claims that she suffered life-threatening injuries or that her campaign has been suspended.
The Associated Press reported that Peltola and family members sustained minor injuries while traveling to the banquet on Saturday, with campaign manager Cheryl Bruce describing them as being in good spirits after the crash. The wire service also confirmed that medical providers recommended rest and that Sunday and Monday campaign appearances would be moved; it did not report serious injuries, identify the other motorist, or provide an official police finding on fault, leaving the campaign’s statement as the clearest verified account of what happened.
The crash comes in the closing stretch of one of the nation’s most closely watched Senate races.
Alaska first, Alaska always.
The fight for the Last Frontier comes down to these final days. We’ve been all across the state to connect with as many communities as possible. Now it’s time to get out the vote for fish, family, freedom.
Let’s win this, Alaska. pic.twitter.com/KvfyUB0YUD
— Mary Peltola (@MaryPeltola) October 25, 2026
Peltola, 53, is attempting to unseat Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan after winning the most votes in Alaska’s August top-four primary.
The November contest will use Alaska’s ranked-choice voting system, with four candidates advancing from the primary to the general election.
Dan Sullivan and his DC insiders have spent millions on dishonest attack ads to distract Alaskans from the truth – Dan is part of a rigged system where politicians get wealthy while we go backwards financially. pic.twitter.com/Q2WWh7LEEU
— Mary Peltola (@MaryPeltola) October 25, 2026
Peltola previously represented Alaska in the U.S. House, winning a 2022 special election before losing the seat to Republican Nick Begich in 2024.
Her Senate bid has focused heavily on personal appearances across the state, making the temporary postponement of two tour stops politically notable even though the campaign is presenting the disruption as brief.
CBS News likewise reported that another driver struck the vehicle carrying Peltola and her family as they traveled to the Alaska Federation of Natives banquet, with the campaign describing the injuries as minor and emphasizing that the family was doing well. Its report placed the crash within Peltola’s challenge to Sullivan and noted that she led the top-four primary; the network did not report a campaign withdrawal or prolonged halt, only the rescheduling of two events while Peltola follows medical advice.
The timing is especially sensitive because Alaska’s vast geography makes travel a central part of statewide campaigning.
Candidates routinely cover enormous distances to reach communities that cannot be treated like stops on a conventional Lower 48 campaign swing.
Peltola’s team has made that travel-intensive strategy part of its message, branding the current run as the Alaska Always Tour and promising visits throughout the state.
For now, the campaign’s message is that the crash is a temporary interruption—not an end to that plan.
The Gateway Pundit, which first brought this assignment to our attention, highlighted the campaign’s Sunday announcement, the postponed Fairbanks and Bethel events, and the political stakes of Peltola’s Senate challenge. Its central factual claims are supported by the campaign’s public statement and independent reporting from the Associated Press and CBS News: another driver hit the vehicle, Peltola and relatives sustained minor injuries, and medical providers advised recovery time.
There is no indication at this time that the crash will keep Peltola off the trail for an extended period.
But with Election Day approaching, even a short pause can matter in a statewide race where every trip requires substantial time and planning.
The most important news, however, is that the injuries were described as minor and that Peltola and her family are recovering.
Further details about the collision, including whether law enforcement issued any citation or identified a cause, had not been released as of Sunday afternoon.
This is a Guest Post from our friends over at WLTReport. View the original article here.

sources.news_title: Alaska Senate Candidate Mary Peltola Injured in Car Crash, Postpones Campaign Events Before Midterms
U.S. Senate candidate Mary Peltola and her family suffer minor injuries in car crash
sources.text:
Alaska’s Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Mary Peltola and her family suffered minor injuries Saturday in a car crash while driving to the Alaska Federation of Natives banquet, her campaign said.
Peltola required medical attention after the accident, which happened when another vehicle crashed into the one transporting Peltola and her family, the campaign said.
Peltola, an Alaska Native and former U.S. representative, is challenging Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan, hoping to become the first Democrat in nearly two decades to represent the state in the Senate. Both candidates have tried to rally support from Alaska Native voters, a key constituency in the high-stakes race that has become one of the most watched in the nation.
On Friday, President Donald Trump — who held a rally in support of Sullivan earlier this month in Wasilla — said he told his administration to sue to block certification of the race if the incumbent loses. The lawsuit cites potential confusion with another candidate who is listed on the ranked choice ballot as Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.
Peltola’s campaign manager, Cheryl Bruce, wrote in a statement that the candidate was in “good spirits” after the accident, but her medical providers recommended she reschedule events Sunday in Fairbanks and Monday in Bethel to recover.
The incident delayed what her campaign announced as the “Alaska Always Tour,” an eight-stop push through the last week before Election Day. Her campaign said she will resume events Tuesday, with a stop in Homer.

sources.text:
Democrat Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola was injured in a car crash, her campaign announced on Sunday.
Peltola suffered non-life-threatening injuries that required medical attention after the vehicle that was transporting her was struck by another driver on Saturday.
Peltola’s camp said events scheduled in Fairbanks and Bethel for Sunday and Monday were postponed due to the car accident.
Peltola Campaign Statement on Upcoming Campaign Stops in Fairbanks and Bethel for the Alaska Always Tour: https://t.co/ZhIzk3Oipk
— Mary Peltola (@MaryPeltola) October 25, 2026
NBC News reported:
Former Rep. Mary Peltola is rescheduling several upcoming campaign events after she and her family sustained “minor” injuries in a car crash, her campaign announced on Sunday.
“Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits. Unfortunately, per the advice of medical professionals, Mary’s upcoming events in Fairbanks and Bethel will be rescheduled for later in the week as she takes time to recover,” Peltola campaign manager Cheryl Bruce said in a statement.
“Mary is disappointed that the accident is delaying the start of her Alaska Always Tour, and she is eager to get back on the campaign trail to speak directly with Alaskans about her plan to take on the rigged system and lower costs for working families,” Bruce added.
Peltola was en route to the Alaska Federation of Natives’ annual banquet on Saturday when a vehicle transporting the candidate and her family was struck by another driver, according to the campaign.
The police department in Anchorage confirmed Sunday that a collision involving three vehicles occurred on Saturday evening and those involved sustained “non-life threatening injuries.”
Alaska’s Senate race has turned into a legal battle after the Democrats used a decoy candidate to confuse voters.
The Justice Department on Friday sued to block Alaska’s Senate certification if incumbent GOP Senator Dan Sullivan loses over the Democrats’ dirty trick to use a ‘decoy’ Dan Sullivan on the ballot.
A Democrat operative worked to register a man named Daniel J. Sullivan as Dan S. Sullivan (the incumbent Senator’s name) as a Republican primary challenger.
The decoy saboteur, Daniel J. Sullivan, is a Democrat and has a team of Democrats working for him, but they registered him as a Republican to cause chaos and confusion during Alaska’s August primary.
After that plan failed to add the decoy Dan Sullivan to the primary ballot over the summer, Daniel J. Sullivan’s name will appear on the Alaska ballot in the general election in November.
The lawsuit is seeking an order to block the Senate election results from being certified “if: (1) Senator Sullivan does not win the election; and (2) had all votes cast for Daniel J. Sullivan been cast instead for Senator Sullivan and Alaska’s rank-choice process played out accordingly, Senator Sullivan would have won the election.”

sources.news_title: Mary Peltola Campaign Gives Update After Candidate Injured in Car Crash
sources.text:
Alaska Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola and members of her family suffered minor injuries in a car crash Saturday while traveling to a campaign event, prompting her campaign to postpone several stops during the final stretch before Election Day.
Peltola required medical attention after another vehicle crashed into the one carrying her and her family as they headed to the Alaska Federation of Natives Annual Banquet, according to her campaign. The wreck disrupted the opening of Peltola’s “Alaska Always Tour,” an eight-stop campaign swing planned for the final week before Election Day.
An Alaska Native and former congresswoman, Peltola is challenging Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in one of the country’s closely watched Senate contests. She is seeking to become the first Democrat in nearly two decades to represent the state in the Senate. Both candidates have sought support from Alaska Native voters, a key constituency in the race.
“Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits,” campaign manager Cheryl Bruce said in a statement. “Unfortunately, per the advice of medical professionals, Mary’s upcoming events in Fairbanks and Bethel will be rescheduled for later in the week as she takes time to recover. Mary is disappointed that the accident is delaying the start of her Alaska Always Tour, and she is eager to get back on the campaign trail to speak directly with Alaskans about her plan to take on the rigged system and lower costs for working families.”
Peltola is expected to resume campaigning Tuesday with a stop in Homer.
What We Know About the Crash Involving Mary Peltola
According to Anchorage police, Peltola’s vehicle was stopped at a red light at O'Malley Road and Lake Otis Parkway when it was rear-ended, pushing it into a third vehicle. Peltola and others in her vehicle were taken to a local hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, while the driver who allegedly struck their vehicle was also hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries. The occupant of the third vehicle refused medical transport, according to Anchorage police.
Police said the crash remains under investigation. A Peltola campaign spokesperson told NBC News the campaign had no reason to believe the incident was politically motivated.
Newsweek has reached out to the Anchorage Police Department and the Peltola campaign via email on Sunday afternoon for comment.
Trump Escalates Fight Over Alaska Senate Race
President Donald Trump has thrown his support behind Sullivan and held a rally for the Republican earlier this month.
Trump also alleged, without providing evidence, that Democrats were trying to siphon votes from Sullivan by supporting Daniel J. Sullivan, a retired schoolteacher and former Forest Service employee who is also running as a Republican.
Trump urged Alaskans to vote “YES” on Ballot Measure 2, which would repeal ranked-choice voting. Alaska’s system eliminates the lowest-performing candidate if no one receives more than 50 percent of first-choice votes, redistributing those ballots according to voters’ subsequent choices until a candidate secures a majority.
The Department of Justice has filed a lawsuit seeking to halt certification of the Senate results if Senator Sullivan does not win, citing potential voter confusion between the two similarly named candidates. On the ballot, the incumbent appears as Dan S. Sullivan and is labeled “Incumbent,” while his challenger appears as Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.
Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. was initially removed from the ballot after Alaska election officials concluded his candidacy was intended to confuse or mislead voters. He challenged that decision and was later restored to the ballot by the courts.
Trump has acknowledged directing the DOJ to pursue the case, telling reporters: "I'm the one that said 'do it,'" as he arrived in Florida Friday afternoon.
The president told reporters Sunday that Alaska’s ballot is illegal because voters don’t know what “incumbent” means.
Attorney General Todd Blanche defended the lawsuit Sunday on CBS News’ Face the Nation, while declining to say whether Trump personally directed him to bring the case.
Murkowski Pushes Back on DOJ Lawsuit
Lisa Murkowski, an Alaska Republican who has frequently broken with Trump, pushed back against the lawsuit Saturday.
“Alaskans don’t need any help voting for their preferred candidates, and the State of Alaska has already handled this by clearly distinguishing the candidates on this year’s ballot,” she wrote on X. “The Department of Justice should never have filed this lawsuit.”
Trump responded by suggesting Murkowski opposed the lawsuit because she wanted Sen. Sullivan to lose votes.
“Murkowski probably wants that to happen, which is why she is against the DOJ filing a Lawsuit in order to stop this impending crime and tragedy,” Trump wrote.
Peltola Holds Narrow Lead in Recent Polls
The dispute comes just days before the November 3 midterms, with the Alaska contest among the races that could determine control of the Senate. Republicans currently hold a 53-47 majority, while Peltola is seeking to become the first Democrat elected to the Senate from Alaska since Mark Begich in 2008.
Recent polling indicates a tight race. An InsiderAdvantage poll showed Peltola leading Sullivan 50 percent to 48 percent in the ranked-choice contest.
A Data for Progress poll similarly showed Peltola ahead, 51 percent to 49 percent, in a simulated final round of ranked-choice voting. The survey put Sullivan’s net favorability at minus 10, with 44 percent viewing him favorably and 54 percent unfavorably. According to Data for Progress, that was his lowest net favorability across its six Alaska surveys since February 2024.
Newsweek reporters and editors used Martyn, our AI assistant, to produce this story. Learn more about Martyn here. Contact Newsweek editors for this story: Anthony Murray and Gabe Whisnant.

sources.text:
Former Rep. Mary Peltola is rescheduling several upcoming campaign events after she and her family sustained “minor” injuries in a car crash, her campaign announced Sunday.
“Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits. Unfortunately, per the advice of medical professionals, Mary’s upcoming events in Fairbanks and Bethel will be rescheduled for later in the week as she takes time to recover,” Peltola campaign manager Cheryl Bruce said in a statement.
“Mary is disappointed that the accident is delaying the start of her Alaska Always Tour, and she is eager to get back on the campaign trail to speak directly with Alaskans about her plan to take on the rigged system and lower costs for working families,” Bruce added.
Peltola was en route to the Alaska Federation of Natives’ annual banquet Saturday when a vehicle transporting the candidate and her family was struck by another driver, according to the campaign. A spokesperson for the campaign said they had no reason to believe the accident had been politically motivated.
The police department in Anchorage confirmed Sunday that a collision involving three vehicles occurred on evening and those involved sustained “non-life threatening injuries.”
Police added that the incident is under investigation.
Peltola, a Democrat, is locked in a competitive Senate race against GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan. She was elected to the House in 2022 but narrowly lost her re-election bid in 2024, the same year that President Donald Trump won the state by 13 percentage points.
Sullivan’s re-election race, in which he’s seeking a third term, is tighter than expected, with Alaska voters tying Trump to high gas and grocery prices resulting from the ongoing war with Iran.
Trump and Vice President JD Vance rallied voters in Alaska separately earlier this month.
Republicans have accused Democrats of recruiting another candidate named Dan Sullivan to run for the Senate, saying that voters may be confused by the presence of two Dan Sullivans on the ballot if they plan to vote for the incumbent senator.
Democrats have not taken credit for recruiting the second Dan Sullivan into the race. He’ll appear on the ballot as Dan J. Sullivan, while the incumbent senator will be identified by his name, political party and a clear notation that he’s the incumbent.
Last week, the Justice Department sued Alaska’s election officials, seeking to block certification of the election if Sen. Dan Sullivan loses. It cited Dan J. Sullivan’s presence on the ballot as a point of “voter confusion.”
On Saturday, Democrats filed a motion urging a federal judge to dismiss the case.

sources.news_title: Alaska Dem Mary Peltola in car crash during final sprint for Senate
sources.text:
Alaska Dem Mary Peltola in car crash during final sprint for Senate
Alaska Senate Democratic hopeful Mary Peltola suffered minor injuries in a car crash Saturday, temporarily sidelining her campaign, according to her team.
Peltola, 53, was en route to the Alaska Federation of Natives Annual Banquet when her vehicle was hit by another car, forcing her to reschedule her campaign events slated for Sunday and Monday, her campaign said.
“Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits,” said Cheryl Bruce, Peltola’s campaign manager, in a statement.
“Mary is disappointed that the accident is delaying the start of her Alaska Always Tour, and she is eager to get back on the campaign trail to speak directly with Alaskans about her plan to take on the rigged system and lower costs for working families,” Bruce said.
Alaska’s Senate race has been deemed one of the seven toss-up contests by Cook Political Report in the battle to control the upper chamber.
Peltola had been embarking on an eight-day “Alaska Always Tour” in the final days before the Nov. 3 election when the accident occurred.
The candidate, who served in Congress from early 2023 through early 2025, has a 1.2 percentage point edge over her rival, incumbent Sen. Dan S. Sullivan (R-Alaska), according to the latest RealClearPolitics aggregate of polls.
The race has faced controversy thanks to retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan’s presence as a hopeful. Dubbed by critics as “Decoy Dan,” he has faced scrutiny for having a near-identical name to the incumbent senator.
Last week, the Justice Department sued to block the certification of Alaska’s Senate race if Sen. Sullivan loses because of “Decoy Dan.”
“Decoy Dan” is registered as a Republican, despite admitting he voted for Democrats in recent presidential election cycles, attended a “No Kings” rally and engaged in other left-leaning activity.

sources.news_title: Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola injured in car crash; postpones campaign events before midterms
sources.text:
Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola injured in car crash; postpones campaign events before midterms
Alaska's Democrat Senate candidate Mary Peltola and her family got minor injuries in a car crash, and her campaign has put some events on hold so she can rest.
Alaska Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola and her family suffered “minor injuries” in a car accident, her campaign said on Sunday.
According to Politico, the crash took place on Saturday night. As per her campaign, Peltola and her family were on their way to the Alaska Federation of Natives Annual Banquet when another driver hit their vehicle. The campaign said the injuries needed medical attention.
“Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits,” Peltola’s campaign manager, Cheryl Bruce, said in a statement.
Also read: Mary Peltola, the former Alaska congresswoman running for the US Senate
Campaign events pushed back
Bruce said Peltola is rescheduling events on the advice of doctors as she takes time to recover.
“Unfortunately, per the advice of medical professionals, Mary’s upcoming events in Fairbanks and Bethel will be rescheduled for later in the week as she takes time to recover,” Bruce said in the statement as per CBS News.
The crash has hit the start of Peltola’s “Alaska Always Tour." It as an eight-community, seven-day campaign swing ahead of the midterms.
As per Politico, the events in Fairbanks and Bethel were planned for Sunday and Monday and will be rescheduled. The campaign said stops in Homer, Kenai, Seward, Juneau, Anchorage and Palmer will go on as planned.
“Mary is disappointed that the accident is delaying the start of her Alaska Always Tour, and she is eager to get back on the campaign trail to speak directly with Alaskans about her plan to take on the rigged system and lower costs for working families,” Bruce said.
Who is Mary Peltola?
Peltola is 53. She is trying to unseat Republican Senator Dan Sullivan and become the first Democrat elected to the Senate since 2008. This comes four years after she became the first Democrat to represent the state in the House in 50 years.
As per CBS News, she was the top vote-getter in the August top-four primary. That sets up the general election against Sullivan and two other candidates under Alaska’s ranked-choice system.
Peltola was born on August 31, 1973, in Anchorage, Alaska. She grew up in rural Alaska along the Kuskokwim River and is Yup’ik, an Alaskan indigenous group. Her mother, Elizabeth Williams, was from the Yup’ik village of Kwethluk. Her father, Ward Sattler, moved to Alaska from Nebraska and worked as a teacher, principal and bush pilot. As a child, she spent time fishing salmon with her father. This later shaped her interest in fisheries and rural Alaskan communities.
Between 1991 and 1998, she studied at the University of Northern Colorado, the University of Alaska Fairbanks, the University of Alaska Southeast and the University of Alaska Anchorage.
She has seven children. Four are her biological children and three are stepchildren, whom she raised with her late husband, Eugene “Buzzy” Peltola Jr. He was a former Alaska regional director for the Bureau of Indian Affairs. He died in a plane crash in September 2023.

sources.text:
Alaska Senate candidate involved in car crash, campaign events postponed
Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola was involved in a car accident that caused the Democrat to postpone two campaign stops during the final week before the midterm elections, her campaign announced on Sunday.
The former congresswoman and her family were traveling to the Alaska Federation of Natives Annual Banquet on Saturday when the vehicle transporting them was struck by another driver, the campaign said in a statement provided to USA Today. The crash caused injuries that required medical treatment, according to the campaign.
“Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits,” campaign manager Cheryl Bruce said.
Two stops on the campaign’s “Alaska Always Tour” scheduled for Sunday and Monday in Fairbanks and Bethel were postponed as Bruce said Peltola was “taking time to recover” under “the advice of medical professionals.”
The statement said the events would be rescheduled in “the coming days” for “later in the week.” Other dates will continue as scheduled. The next event is scheduled for Peltola is a rally in Homer on Oct. 27, according to the campaign’s website.
Peltola in key Senate race
Peltola is in a key race for control of the Senate against Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan. She would be the first Democrat elected from the state since 2008.
The Alaska Senate race is one of the nation’s most competitive Senate contests and one of seven races in a state Trump won in 2024 now rated “toss up” by the Cook Political Report.
Sullivan has trailed the Peltola in available polling of the race.
The Trump administration sued on Oct. 23 to block the certification of the race if Sullivan does not win, alleging that another candidate on the ballot with an almost identical name may confuse voters and violate the senator’s duties under the National Voter Registration Act’s aim to “protect the integrity of the electoral process.”
President Donald Trump told reporters that he directed the suit, saying, “I was the one who said to do it.”
Peltola called the lawsuit “desperate” and “clearly corruption.”
“It’s sending a message that Dan Sullivan does not believe that Alaskans are sophisticated enough to know exactly who they’re voting for and what the implication of their vote is,” Peltola said in an interview with MS NOW on Oct. 23.
Attorney General Todd Blanche, a former personal attorney for Trump, defended the lawsuit Oct. 25 in an appearance on CNN’s “State of the Union.”
“Putting aside whether we’re going to win or lose in the courts, putting aside what the Alaskan Supreme Court has done. In our system, we should not have a candidate who has to worry about another candidate being on the ballot for no other reason to confuse voters,” Blanche said.
Contributing: Jay Stahl, Emily R. Condon, USA TODAY
